Article Title: 'Deafening silence from PM': Congress targets Centre over reported 'face-offs' along Arunachal border
Article Text:
ITBP chief flags ‘ongoing’ China faceoff along Arunachal border

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of remaining silent on reported face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh. The party also alleged that the government had made ‘concessions’ to Beijing and failed to adequately address concerns over border security.In a post on X, the opposition party criticised PM over his interactions with Chinese president Xi Jinping at the BRICS summit, saying the prime minister was seen joking with Xi even as Indian troops reportedly faced tensions along the border."Instead of showing China the "red eye," Narendra Modi was seen joking around with Chinese President Xi Jinping—at the BRICS summit", it wrote.The Congress also alleged that reports of clashes with Chinese soldiers had been suppressed since July.The party's handle shared the video of the ITBP chief and wrote, “Modi has abandoned our soldiers every time, betrayed the country, and washed his hands of responsibility. Sometimes giving China a clean chit, sometimes abandoning control of patrolling points and the country's land. He called Prime Minister Narendra Modi a “weak prime minister” and accused him of causing immense damage to the country.The criticism follows remarks by Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor, who said on Thursday that the force’s newly raised Shaurya commando unit had demonstrated its capabilities during ongoing face-offs with China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) at multiple locations in Arunachal Pradesh.Kapoor said the specialised commandos would be deployed across every border battalion as the ITBP strengthens its combat readiness along the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control (LAC). The force is also expanding its modernisation drive, with greater emphasis on specialised training and emerging warfare technologies.Meanwhile, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh separately cited media reports about the recent face-offs, questioning the Centre’s silence on the developments. He alleged that India had made concessions to China and raised concerns over reports of lost patrolling points in Arunachal Pradesh.“While the self-styled Vishwaguru’s calibrated concessions to China continue, the DG, ITBP, has lauded—and rightly so—its performance in recent face-offs with the PLA in Arunachal Pradesh, on which there has been a deafening silence from the PM and his establishment,” Ramesh wrote .He added that local residents had reported the loss of patrolling points, drawing a parallel with developments in Ladakh.Ramesh also flagged China’s renaming of places in Arunachal Pradesh and the construction of a reported 60,000-MW dam, arguing that these developments posed risks to India’s ecological and water security.On the economic front, the Congress leader claimed that India’s trade deficit with China had reached a record $112 billion in 2025-26, compared with $99 billion in the previous financial year. He criticised the government’s Make in India initiative, writing that it had effectively become “Import from China”, and described the widening trade gap as a threat to economic security.The Congress also invoked Modi’s June 19, 2020, remarks following the Galwan Valley clash, in which 20 Indian soldiers were killed. Ramesh quoted the prime minister as saying that no one had entered Indian territory and that no Indian post was under another country’s control.
Article Summary: The Congress accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of remaining silent on reported face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh. The party also alleged that the government had made ‘concessions’ to Beijing and failed to adequately address concerns over border security.

Article Title: 'Disgrace at so many levels': Shashi Tharoor reacts to removal of Raihan Vadra's photos from exhibition
Article Text:
Tharoor backs Raihan Vadra, says protest photos are not political in themselves

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday criticised the removal of photographs from Raihan Vadra's exhibition at Bikaner House in New Delhi, saying the move had damaged India's global reputation as a freedom-loving democracy and raised serious concerns over freedom of expression.In a post on X, Tharoor described the incident as a "disgrace at so many levels", arguing that photographs documenting protest demonstrations depicted events and did not necessarily convey political positions."This is a disgrace at so many levels," Thiruvananthapuram MP said, listing his objections to the decision to remove the photographs from the exhibition, "No Idea Is Final".He said the images documented events that had already received widespread public and media attention, questioning why photographs of demonstrations should be considered political content simply because they depicted protests."The images are of events that have already been burned into the public consciousness, and many of the photos would have echoed similar images that the public has already seen in the media and online," Tharoor said, adding that "While Bikaner House is free to have a policy against political stands, photographs of a protest demonstration are a depiction of an event and not political in themselves; they would almost certainly have passed muster had the matter been brought to a court as an issue of freedom of expression.He further alleged that the decision had hurt India's international image."And worst of all, this censorship has driven one more nail into the coffin of India's global reputation as a freedom-loving democracy," the Congress MP said.Tharoor also pointed out that the controversy had brought significant attention to Raihan Vadra's photographic work, potentially exposing it to a much wider audience than the exhibition would otherwise have reached."Anyway, the publicity this episode has received will have reached a far larger audience, in Delhi and worldwide, than the exhibition itself might have, had it been allowed to proceed undisturbed. I thank heavy-handed officials for giving a well-deserved boost to the photographic talents and career of Raihan Vadra," Tharoor said.The row began after Raihan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, alleged that Bikaner House management had asked him to remove several photographs from his exhibition shortly before its scheduled opening. According to him, the images included photographs documenting student protests and two pictures of the Indian national flag.The Bikaner House Management Society said certain photographs did not comply with its policy and that their removal had been requested. It maintained that photographs meeting the venue's guidelines continued to be displayed.The incident sparked a political confrontation, with Congress leaders criticising the decision as an infringement on artistic expression, while the BJP maintained that exhibitions must follow the venue's rules.Amid the controversy, Keralam chief minister VD Satheesan offered to host the exhibition in its entirety, saying the state would be proud to welcome “No Idea Is Final”, with "no exclusions, no exceptions".However, Kerala BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar questioned the offer, alleging preferential treatment for Raihan Vadra and asking whether ordinary young people received similar attention to their rights and work.
Article Summary: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor criticises removal of photographs from exhibition. Tharoo says photographs documenting protest demonstrations depicted events and did not necessarily convey political positions. He says the move had damaged India's global reputation as a freedom-loving democracy.

Article Title: Sudan’s RSF fighters deliberately targeted atleast 43 hospitals during el-Fasher siege: Report
Article Text:
A recent BBC investigation has uncovered alarming evidence of the RSF's assault on numerous healthcare facilities in el-Fasher, Sudan.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A BBC investigation has uncovered evidence suggesting that Sudan’s paramilitary rapid support forces (RSF) systematically targeted and dismantled healthcare facilities in el-Fasher during a prolonged siege and the subsequent capture of the Darfur city a year ago.UN high commissioner for human rights Volker Türk described the findings as “deeply disturbing”. He said repeated RSF attacks on civilian infrastructure, including medical facilities, constituted serious violations of international humanitarian law and could amount to war crimes.The RSF has rejected the allegations. The group’s health minister dismissed the findings as propaganda, alleging that Sudan’s national army and its allies were attempting to damage the paramilitary force’s reputation.Drawing on accounts from people who were present in el-fasher, the BBC identified details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and other healthcare facilities between May 2024 and October 2025. Some sites were reportedly struck multiple times.International law prohibits attacks on medical facilities and healthcare workers during armed conflicts.Medical workers killed, injured or abductedThe investigation also documents the impact of the conflict on medical personnel in the western Sudanese city.According to the BBC’s data, 120 healthcare workers were injured, 55 were killed and 10 were forcibly disappeared or abducted between April 2023 and October 2025.Dr Muhamed Suliman, a surgeon who worked in el-fasher during the siege, told the BBC that the RSF sought to force hospitals out of operation.“The RSF [were] trying to evacuate the hospitals, to put them out of service because the health system is the cornerstone of any city or any state,” he said.Suliman alleged that attacks were intended to make it impossible for civilians to remain in the affected areas, describing the campaign as intense, deliberate and planned.El-Fasher siege marked a brutal phase of Sudan’s warThe investigation was published a year after the fall of el-fasher, one of the most devastating episodes in Sudan’s civil war, which erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and the country’s military.Both sides have faced accusations of attacking healthcare facilities.In March 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) condemned a bombing at al-Daein hospital in eastern Darfur, an area controlled by the RSF. The attack killed dozens of people and forced the facility to close. Sudan’s military was believed to have carried out the drone strikes, but it denied responsibility.Responding to a BBC inquiry, the WHO described the events in el-fasher as “one of the clearest and most severe examples of the wider impact of the conflict on health care in Sudan”.UN investigators have also said the violence in el-fasher bore the “hallmarks of genocide”. The city’s population includes non-Arab communities that have faced attacks amid longstanding ethnic tensions, with Arab militias now forming the backbone of the RSF.The BBC investigation provides a detailed chronology of attacks on healthcare facilities during the prolonged siege, shedding further light on the conflict’s impact on medical services and civilians.
Article Summary: UN high commissioner for human rights described the findings as 'deeply disturbing' At least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and other healthcare facilities between May 2024 and October 2025. 120 healthcare workers were injured, 55 were killed and 10 were forcibly disappeared or abducted.

Article Title: Chennai may receive heavy rain from today
Article Text:
From Friday, heavy monsoon rain is likely to return to the city, with the IMD issuing a yellow alert for heavy rainfall of 6- 12cm in 24 hours in the city and neighbouring districts over the next four days





CHENNAI: Sunshine and cloudy skies interspersed throughout the day, followed by light rain in parts of the city on Thursday night. From Friday, heavy monsoon rain is likely to return to the city, with the IMD issuing a yellow alert for heavy rainfall of 6- 12cm in 24 hours in the city and neighbouring districts over the next four days.The rainfall is associated with a low-pressure area that formed over the southwest Bay of Bengal and has since moved to the Comorin region and adjoining parts of southern Tamil Nadu and Kerala . Its associated cyclonic circulation extends up to 5.8km above mean sea level, helping lift moist air, which cools and condenses to form rain-bearing clouds. The system and atmospheric instability are expected to sustain rainfall over several parts of the state.The system may move northwards, bringing rain to Chennai and surrounding areas, an IMD official said. The city may receive moderate to heavy rain with thunderstorms and lightning on Friday. Cloudy skies are likely to keep maximum temperatures at 31-32°C and minimum temperatures at 25-26°C, according to the IMD.The agency has forecast heavy rain in 26 districts on Friday, including Chennai and Tiruvallur. From Oct 24 to 26, the warning will also cover Chengelpet and Kancheepuram, along with several delta and interior districts.An orange alert for heavy to very heavy rain has been issued for districts along the Western Ghats from Oct 23 to 26.
Article Summary: The IMD has issued a yellow alert for heavy rainfall of 6- 12cm in 24 hours in the city and neighbouring districts over the next four days. The agency has forecast heavy rain in 26 districts on Friday, including Chennai and Tiruvallur. Cloudy skies are likely to keep maximum temperatures at 31-32°C.

Article Title: ‘There is nothing wrong with regime change in a democracy’: Neha Bora tells Delhi HC, denies role in CJP protest call, court reserves order on police peace bond notice
Article Text:
Neha Bora (, president of All India Students' Association, is contesting a police notice issued against her





NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora told Delhi High Court Thursday that she was not involved in the Cockroach Janta Party's Oct 16 protest call at Central Park in Connaught Place and had organised a separate gathering at Mandi House.Her counsel also said that there was nothing wrong with seeking regime change in a democracy, when the police's counsel pointed to Bora's presence in a news conference where "regime change" was mentioned.Bora has contested a police notice asking her to execute a "peace" bond before a special executive magistrate. Her submission was before Justice Subramonium Prasad who, after hearing her counsel and police for nearly three hours, reserved the order. The verdict will be pronounced Friday. Bora has to appear before a special executive magistrate Saturday.She has sought a direction from the court to police to not take any coercive action against her.Her plea has pointed out factual incorrectness in the notice, which has associated her with a CJP protest, when she was present at a protest at Mandi House.Additional solicitor-general Chetan Sharma, who represented Delhi Police, drew the court's attention to the press conference attended by Bora and others.He highlighted that in the joint sitting it was announced that "yeh regime change ki ladai hai and hum regime change karake rahenge (this is a fight for regime change and we will get the regime changed)".To this, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, who was representing Bora, said the statement cannot be attributed to her. He then said that "there is nothing wrong with regime change in a democracy."The law officer objected to this. "You were part of that news conference. I will take exception to this. A regime change will happen by votes, not by lumpen elements congregating in... Delhi," he said.Bora's lawyer argued that there was no application of mind or independent opinion by the special executive magistrate while issuing the notice. It was a mere cut-and-paste job that was done mechanically, he said. "According to the notice what I have done -- shouting loudly at the protest at the roundabout of Mandi House. You were involved in protest-related activities in and around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders. You instigated people to participate in unauthorised demonstration at Central Park, Connaught Place... and also hoist the national flag without obtaining valid permission," the counsel said. "Maybe they need some instruction on law that we don't need permission to hoist the national flag," he said.According to the notice, there was apprehension of breach of public peace and tranquillity within the jurisdiction of the SEM's court.Challenging the notice, Bora said it does not meet the essential requirements as mandated by the law.The court asked the police if it can hold off on enforcing the notice till the high court takes a call, but the ASG said if the petitioner is ready to give an undertaking to the court that she will not breach peace, he was ready to give an undertaking.The ASG said there were 12 violations by Bora. "It is not a simple case of an innocent woman," he said.
Article Summary: All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora is contesting a police notice issued against her. Bora has to appear before a special executive magistrate Saturday. Her plea has pointed out factual incorrectness in the notice, which has associated her with a CJP protest.

Article Text:
It expressed concern over scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors.

NEW DELHI: Indian Medical Association has written to I&B ministry to urgently review the promotional content of Sunny Deol-starrer ‘Suryaa – Ant Se Aarambh Tak’, alleging that it generalises corruption in the medical profession and depicts violence against healthcare workers in ways that could erode public trust and put doctors’ safety at risk.In a letter, dated Oct 22, to I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak sought an impartial review of the promo video for the upcoming film and appropriate corrective measures from its makers. It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of National Medical Commission.IMA flagged what it described as the risk of portraying corruption and unethical practices as representative of the medical fraternity. While stressing that individual wrongdoing must be investigated and punished, it said the actions of a few should not tarnish the reputation of doctors as a community.It expressed concern over scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nurses and hospital staff, particularly when such acts appear heroic or justified.It warned that such portrayals could normalise violence against healthcare professionals, who already face safety challenges in hospitals.The letter said such depictions could fuel mistrust between patients and doctors, weakening the cooperation essential for treatment and healthcare delivery. It also warned that such negative portrayals could demoralise medical students and discourage young people from entering the profession.IMA said that while it respected freedom of creative expression, the same should be exercised responsibly when healthcare worker safety and public confidence in essential services are at stake.
Article Summary: Indian Medical Association has written to I&B ministry to urgently review the promotional content of Sunny Deol-starrer ‘Suryaa – Ant Se Aarambh Tak’ It alleges that it generalises corruption in the medical profession and depicts violence against healthcare workers.

NEW DELHI/SRINAGAR: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk accused Centre of backtracking on an understanding reached with Ladakh groups in May 2026, including on a UT-level elected body, calling the failure to hold talks in Delhi on Thursday “yet another betrayal of trust”.“The govt had said Ladakh lacked resources for full statehood. Article Title: Resignation by Justice Yashwant Varma may end Lok Sabha proceedings
Article Text:
Justice Yashwant Varma’s name still figuring on the list of judges on the HC website had bolstered the view.

Further action may be considered in accordance with law: Report

NEW DELHI: Ongoing proceedings in Lok Sabha for removal of Justice Yashwant Varma, who was indicted by an inquiry committee over the discovery of huge sums of unaccounted money from his residence, are likely to be called off due to the view that his resignation has rendered the exercise unnecessary.The three-member panel led by SC judge Aravind Kumar was allowed to complete its probe despite Varma, a judge in Allahabad HC, resigning on April 10. With Speaker Om Birla accepting the report, it was believed that Parliament would proceed with impeachment proceedings to send out a message against judicial corruption.Justice Yashwant Varma’s name still figuring on the list of judges on the HC website had bolstered the view. However, sources said legal opinion, backed by a court verdict, that an HC judge’s resignation comes into effect as soon as he resigns may prevail in what was earlier seen as a legal grey area.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, who had constituted the inquiry committee, is likely to consult different political parties before making a pronouncement on the issue in Parliament’s next session. While the committee’s report was tabled in LS and RS on Aug 12, there was no discussion amid the bitter stand-off between the opposition and govt.The committee in its report had indicted Justice Varma for the recovery of wads of 500-rupee notes in his official residence at Delhi, its unexplained disappearance, and an evasive judge failing to explain “presence, source or ownership” of the huge money. It had recommended further action.The report recommended “such further action as may be considered in accordance with law” against him. It said his explanation “remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against the evidence of independent official witnesses and corroborative material”.If Varma is considered to have resigned, a likelihood, he will also no longer enjoy the legal immunity given to the higher judiciary. It remains to be seen if govt considers criminal investigation against him under anti-corruption laws over an incident which had drawn widespread outrage.
Article Summary: The three-member panel led by SC judge Aravind Kumar was allowed to complete its probe despite Varma, a judge in Allahabad HC, resigning on April 10. With Speaker Om Birla accepting the report, it was believed that Parliament would proceed with impeachment proceedings.

Article Title: ‘No permission needed to hoist national flag’: Neha Bora tells Delhi HC, challenges police notice
Article Text:
‘Don’t need permission to hoist Tricolour’: AISA chief tells Delhi High Court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora on Thursday told the Delhi high court that no permission was required to hoist the national flag, while challenging a police notice directing her to execute a bond to maintain peace.The Delhi police objected to the maintainability of Bora's petition challenging the notice, which asked her to execute a "peace" bond before a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM).The Delhi High Court will pass an order on Friday evening on Neha Bora’s plea challenging a police notice directing her to execute a “peace” bond.Bora on Monday had moved the Delhi High Court challenging a police notice directing her to execute a bond before a Special Executive Magistrate for “keeping peace”.Bora, who has been at the forefront of recent protests against alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety “for keeping peace for a period of enquiry.”Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.In her petition, Bora has argued that the police notice is vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by any material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace. It also fails to specify the “period, occasion or event in relation to which breach is apprehended”, the plea stated.She had described the proceedings as a “colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution”.According to the petition, the police initiated proceedings before the magistrate citing alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and alleged attempts to instigate people to join a protest at Connaught Place on the same day.“The impugned notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, CP on Oct 16. The petitioner’s call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House,” Bora’s petition said.The development comes after the SEM court at Mandir Marg Police Station ordered the release of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on October 21, after they furnished personal bonds and surety bonds and gave written undertakings to maintain peace.SEM Ritu Raj directed the two activists to furnish personal bonds and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each until the conclusion of the inquiry. The court noted that they had furnished the required bonds and that the sureties had been questioned before their release was ordered."In view of overall facts and circumstances, the respondents are directed to furnish personal bonds and surety bonds in the sum of Rs.50,000 until the conclusion of enquiry," the SEM court ordered.After verifying the sureties prima facie, the court directed their release and issued a warrant to the superintendent of Tihar Jail for compliance.The court also directed the investigating officer to submit a verification report on the sureties at the next hearing. Das, Ranka and their sureties were asked to remain present on the next date of hearing.Emphasising the conditions of their release, the court said, "Needless to mention, the respondents shall appear before this Court on every date of hearing and shall maintain law and order and will not breach peace / public tranquillity of the area and shall strictly adhere to the terms of their bonds and voluntary undertaking given today. The inquiry in the matter shall continue in accordance with law."The matter has been listed for further proceedings on October 23 at 3 pm.During the hearing, Das and Ranka voluntarily submitted written undertakings promising not to breach the peace. They also agreed not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law and said any protests they undertake would comply with the law.The court observed that the immediate measures under Section 135(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to prevent a breach of peace or disturbance of public tranquillity could be adequately ensured through the bonds and written undertakings."Hence, further judicial custody does not appear to be necessary at this stage, particularly after written undertakings before this Court," the court observed.Advocates Abhik Chimni and Abhisht Hela appeared for Das and Ranka.
Article Summary: The Delhi High Court will pass an order on Friday evening on Neha Bora’s plea challenging a police notice directing her to execute a “peace” bond. Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday stressed the urgent need for cessation of hostilities in West Asia in a phone conversation with Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu The talks took place days before the Israeli general elections, the first since the Oct 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attacks and Israel’s military response. Netanyahu said he invited Modi to light the ceremonial torch alongside Indian pilot Smit Machchhar for Israel’s Independence Day celebrations next year.Machchhar, a pilot for flydubai, sustained injuries during an attack by the Omani co-pilot on a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight on Sept 30. Modi did not mention Netanyahu’s invitation in his post on the conversation.“We exchanged views on developments in West Asia and underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region,” Modi said on X.In his own version of the conversation, Netanyahu did not mention the West Asia situation but said India and Israel were fighting terrorism together. “I spoke with my friend, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and invited him to light the torch alongside a brave Indian pilot on Israel’s Independence Day,” Netanyahu said on X.“Modi thanked me for the invitation and said that on land and in the air, India and Israel are fighting terrorism together. He also commended the strong and decades-old ties between us,” he added.
Article Summary: The talks took place days before the Israeli general elections. Netanyahu said he invited Modi to light the ceremonial torch alongside Indian pilot Smit Machchhar for Israel’s Independence Day celebrations next year.Machchhar, a pilot for flydubai, sustained injuries during an attack by the Omani co-pilot on a Tel Aviv-bound flight on Sept 30.

NEW DELHI: India slammed Pakistan at the United Nations, questioning Islamabad's record on religious freedom and the protection of minorities while pointing out its failure to safeguard vulnerable communities at home despite criticising New Delhi.Speaking during an interactive dialogue with the UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Religion or Belief on funeral rights in exceptional circumstances on Thursday, India's first secretary to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, said, "In Pakistan, the number of minorities is shrinking, and their rights are regularly abused. A state that cannot ensure the safety of its own minorities has no standing to lecture India. "She also said human suffering should not be used to serve political interests and called for a more impartial approach to reporting violations of religious freedom.The remarks come against the backdrop of concerns over alleged forced conversions, abductions and marriages involving minority girls in Pakistan, particularly in Sindh.Separately, experts cited by the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights warned that coercion and weak legal safeguards were enabling forced conversions through marriage, particularly among Hindu and Christian communities.The experts emphasised that conversion must be voluntary and that child marriage undermines consent under international law.The Indian representative also questioned the report's emphasis on the funeral rights of terrorists, arguing that the suffering of victims and their families should not be overlooked.She then invoked the 1999 Kargil conflict to challenge Pakistan's position on burials and religious rights, saying Islamabad had refused to accept the bodies of some of its soldiers killed in combat.“It is deeply ironic that a state that did not even accept the bodies of its own soldiers who were killed in combat in 1999 in Kargil, unabashedly speaks with fervour on faith, religious freedom and burials,” Mangalanandan said.She added that the Indian Army had buried several Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic customs.“Let me remind them, it was the Indian Army that buried a number of Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic rites,” she said.Mangalanandan also hit out at Pakistan over its comments on Jammu and Kashmir, urging it to turn its attention to areas under its own occupation.“Pakistan's deep obsession with what is happening in the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir should be actually directed at the developments that are underway in the parts of Jammu and Kashmir under its illegal occupation, such as Rawalakot,” she said.
Article Summary: India's first secretary to the UN questioned Pakistan's record on religious freedom and the protection of minorities. She questioned the report's approach to religious discrimination during the COVID-19 pandemic and its advocacy for the funeral rights of terrorists. Bhavika Mangalanandan also hit out at Pakistan over its comments on Jammu and Kashmir.

JAMMU: A Jammu court has imposed two life sentences and fines of Rs 2 lakh on Mohammed Sharief, a terrorist who gunned down three members of a family, including a six-month-old infant, in Ramban district’s Gool area over 21 years ago.In his order on Wednesday, principal sessions judge Ramban Ajay Kumar Gupta rejected defence arguments that the attack had taken place more than two decades ago when Sharief was young, his long incarceration and possibility of rehabilitation.Besides the life sentences, the court imposed two separate terms of 10 years on Sharief under various sections pertaining to murder and arms act offences. “All sentences shall run concurrently, while the period already spent in custody shall be set off in accordance with law,” the judge said.The court ordered that the fines be paid to those injured in the July 2005 terror attack and directed J&K State Legal Services Authority to provide compensation to heirs of the deceased and the survivors.Judge Gupta rejected defence arguments about the testimony of two injured eyewitnesses, saying they were reliable and corroborated by medical and other evidence. Defective investigations or delay in recording statements could not automatically result in acquittal when credible evidence otherwise established the accused’s guilt beyond reasonable doubt, the judge said.Public prosecutor Wajid Ahmed pressed for maximum punishment under law, contending that the murder of three innocent family members, including the baby, and the use of an AK-47 rifle warranted a stringent sentence.The court considered aggravating and mitigating circumstances and held that although the crime was extremely grave, the case did not warrant the death penalty under the rarest of rare principle.

Article Title: Indian diaspora could pay price for West’s immigration backlash, warns Sushant Sareen
Article Text:

Why Indians could pay the price

Is the West paying for its own mistakes?

Faultline

US President Donald Trump has blamed immigration for the recent unrest in France and urged President Emmanuel Macron to close the country’s borders, reigniting a wider debate over migration, integration and the future of Western societies.But the backlash could also hurt Indians who have built successful lives abroad through legal migration, strategic affairs expert Sushant Sareen has warned.“The law breakers don't care anyways but it's the guys who follow the law who will also get crushed,” Sareen said in an interview on Faultline, hosted by Ananya Dasgupta.Trump has described France’s unrest as a consequence of immigration and warned that Europe risks decline unless it tightens its borders. Macron, however, has rejected attempts by foreign leaders to blame migrants for the violence, pointing to the exploitation of France’s domestic tensions for political gain.Sareen said the Indian diaspora had established a reputation for success in countries such as the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.“The Indian diaspora wherever it went it made a success of itself,” he said.However, he argued that this reputation could come under pressure as anti-immigration sentiment grows.Referring to Canada, Sareen alleged that criminal activity involving some members of the Indian community, including people he linked to Khalistani networks, had damaged the image of the wider diaspora.His concern is that Indians unconnected with such activities could also face the consequences of a broader backlash against migrants.Sareen sees the immigration debate as part of a wider crisis facing Western societies. He argued that governments had failed to manage integration and address tensions around migration, leaving established political and social models under strain.“Multiculturalism has collapsed,” he said, describing what he sees as the failure of the Western approach to managing cultural diversity.Yet Western economies continue to need migrant workers, particularly as populations age and employers face labour shortages. Sareen said governments must rethink their immigration systems, including how long migrants can stay and what rights they should have.For Indians hoping to study, work or settle abroad, tougher visa rules could complicate future plans. Those already settled overseas could also face uncertainty if immigration becomes a proxy for wider anxieties about jobs, identity and cultural change.The contradiction is that Western countries need foreign talent even as political pressure to restrict immigration grows.For India, the stakes extend beyond visa policies. If the West responds to its immigration crisis by treating migrant communities as a single group, law-abiding Indians who have contributed to their host countries could find themselves paying the price.Watchwith Ananya Dasgupta and Sushant Sareen as they discuss the France crisis, the West’s immigration trap, the growing backlash and why Indians could pay the price.

For Indians hoping to study, work or settle abroad, tougher visa rules could complicate future plans.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Nishikant Dubey on Thursday alleged that opposition-led protests in India were part of a conspiracy to destabilise the country.Addressing a press conference, Dubey questioned Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s alleged links with US lawmakers Ilhan Omar and Ro Khanna, while raising concerns over foreign funding, cryptocurrency and online gambling.Dubey alleged that foreign organisations and individuals were backing protests in an attempt to bring about a change of government in India, and claimed that Congress leaders were working in coordination with foreign elements.“All these people - whoever is in the leadership of the Congress party, whoever the opposition is - are all working together with foreign powers to not change the regime, but to break the country,” Dubey said.Questioning Rahul Gandhi’s overseas engagements, BJP MP Nishikant Dubey alleged that the Congress leader had met individuals who, according to him, were working against India’s interests.“I said in Parliament that under the guise of the Soros Foundation, he meets Ilhan Omar and Ro Khanna,” Dubey said, referring to the US lawmakers.He also questioned the Congress over Rahul’s alleged links with individuals associated with online gambling, cryptocurrency and artificial intelligence, and asked whether any of them had participated in the Congress leader’s Bharat Jodo Yatra or other journeys."My question to Congress is - Regarding Neville Roy Singham, the cartels involved in online gambling, artificial intelligence, and cryptocurrency—with which individuals from these circles has Rahul Gandhi met over the past five years? Which of these individuals have participated in his 'Bharat Jodo Yatra' or other such journeys? Moreover, whenever he travels abroad, with which of these elements does he meet, and what kind of plans do they devise to destabilise the country?" he added.Dubey also questioned whether Sam Pitroda had any role in what he described as alleged conspiracies to destabilise India. He sought details of Gandhi’s meetings during overseas visits and asked who among those he had met was associated with the Bharat Jodo Yatra.The BJP MP further referred to US congressional documents that he claimed raised concerns about foreign influence, protests and technology-related issues. He alleged that cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence and online gambling could be exploited by foreign actors to influence political movements.“The future ahead is of artificial intelligence, to destroy the entire world's economy there is cryptocurrency, and the third is online gambling,” he said, calling for greater scrutiny of these areas.Dubey also defended the government's approach to regulating online gambling and cryptocurrency, stating that online gambling had been banned and cryptocurrency did not have legal tender status in India. He said the government had taken steps to address concerns related to these activities.The BJP MP also criticised the ongoing protests in Delhi, particularly demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, alleging that they were disrupting public life.His remarks came after Delhi Police summoned Cockroach Janata Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka following their release from judicial custody by a Special Executive Magistrate court. Their release was subject to undertakings to maintain peace and comply with the law.The development comes as a Fox News Digital investigation titled ‘Global Chaos Inc Grows to 101 Groups’ identified 101 organisations across nine countries that it described as part of a “red-green protest ecosystem”, referring to Islamist and communist groups.The report also flagged Indian Alliance Paris (IAP), a France-based organisation, alleging that it was “connecting French and Indian protest messaging” and was “partnered with the People’s Forum in Manhattan”.It also cited an October 16 briefing by Progressive International that grouped protests in France, Spain, India and Albania, asking whether the “new rebellions can acquire the organised power to change the conditions that produced them?”. The organisation stated: “These are the forces that Progressive International is working to support and connect.”The report’s references to India come amid scrutiny of Rahul Gandhi’s overseas engagements. During his 2024 visit to the United States, the Congress leader and Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition met several US lawmakers at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington. The meeting was hosted by Congressman Bradley James Sherman and attended by Ilhan Omar, Ro Khanna, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Barbara Lee and others.Omar, a Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, has drawn criticism in India over her visit to Pakistan in 2022, during which she met then-Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and former prime minister Imran Khan and travelled to Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). India condemned the visit, describing it as “narrow-minded politics”. Reports at the time said the Pakistani government sponsored her trip and covered her accommodation and expenses.Omar was also among the US lawmakers who boycotted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s address to a joint session of Congress.
Article Summary: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey accuses Congress of colluding with foreign powers. Dubey questions Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s alleged links with US lawmakers Ilhan Omar and Ro Khanna. He also raises concerns over foreign funding, cryptocurrency and online gambling.

Article Title: ‘Anti-Indian hate is exploding’: US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi flags rising anti-Hindu hate online

US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi on Wednesday (local time) raised concerns over rising anti-Indian, anti-South Asian and anti-Hindu hate on social media, accusing major technology companies of profiting from online hostility and calling on Congress to hold them accountable.In a post on X, Krishnamoorthi said, "Anti-Indian hate is exploding on social media, and Big Tech is profiting from it. These companies have no incentive to stop the hatred they help spread. Congress must hold them accountable."He alleged that social media platforms were failing to adequately monitor hateful content, citing an increase of more than 240 per cent in posts promoting anti-South Asian hate.In a video attached to the post, Krishnamoorthi said, "Big Tech is not policing their social media platforms where there's been an explosion of anti-South Asian, anti-Indian, anti-Hindu hate. I'll just give you one statistic: the number of X posts, posts on X or tweets, basically touting anti-South Asian hate has increased by more than 240 per cent over a very short period of time.""And, unfortunately, Big Tech is profiting off of this hate. They have no incentive right now to decrease it. And so we have to at this point, at the federal level, make sure that they face the full consequences of not taking action," he added.His remarks come amid growing concerns over online hostility towards South Asian communities and follow an attempted shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois, on October 11.Krishnamoorthi was worshipping at the temple with his family when the alleged attack took place. He subsequently led 105 members of Congress, including every Indian American member of Congress, in urging FBI director Kash Patel to investigate the incident as a potential federal hate crime.According to prosecutors, 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis, a self-identified neo-Nazi, allegedly attempted to shoot a man outside the temple, but his rifle jammed. He fled the scene and later communicated plans to return. A coworker alerted the police, who arrested him that day.Prosecutors allege that Paporakis had authored an eight-page white supremacist manifesto describing violence against people of Indian descent at a Hindu place of worship.In their letter to Patel, the lawmakers wrote, "The alleged combination of targeted racial hatred, a religious setting, and preparations for mass violence demands a comprehensive federal response. We appreciate the FBI’s reported assistance to local investigators and urge the Bureau to ensure that potential hate-crime violations receive explicit attention."The lawmakers also sought details on whether the FBI was examining possible racial, ethnic and religious bias in the Aurora case, whether online platforms or other individuals had facilitated the alleged plot, and what measures the Bureau was taking to address credible threats against Indian Americans, Hindu Americans and other South Asian communities.The letter further stated, "We believe such messaging risks lending governmental legitimacy to racial and religious stereotyping. Federal agencies should make clear that debates over immigration or public safety never justify collective suspicion of Indian, Sikh, Hindu, or other South Asian communities."The lawmakers requested a written response to their questions by October 29, to the extent permitted by the ongoing investigation.Earlier, on October 20, Krishnamoorthi told news agency ANI that the US was becoming increasingly polarised, alleging that rhetoric from senior government officials was contributing to hostility towards minority communities."Well, yes, I do think that the America of today is more polarised than ever before," he said. He added that leaders at the highest levels of government were targeting groups, including Muslims, Indians and gay people, and "villainising people".Citing a controversial post by the department of homeland security targeting a Sikh man, Krishnamoorthi said, "I mean, the best example of that was the Department of Homeland Security tweet on their official account targeting a quote, unquote, 'Mr. Singh,' and saying, you know, 'self-deport or else. And predictably, one week later, a gentleman named Mr. Singh, a Sikh truck driver, was stabbed 17 times, came within inches of his life.The DHS post, which was later deleted, featured a Transformers-themed cartoon depicting an Indian Sikh man alongside the phrase "Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh” and the words “Self deport or find out".Calling for action against hate crimes, Krishnamoorthi said, "And this is what has to stop. If we're going to stop this horrible rash of hate, it has to stop at the top.""And once that happens, I think things become better, although we at all levels of government have to stand together against it," he added.
Article Summary: Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi raises concerns over rising anti-Indian, anti- South Asian and anti-Hindu hate on social media. Alleges that social media platforms are failing to adequately monitor hateful content. Comes amid growing concerns over online hostility towards South Asian communities.
