Article Title: How a bullet’s twists and turns saved man shot during Tiger Shroff attack
Article Text:
Umesh Chauhan was shot during an attack aimed at Tiger Shroff

How the bullet travelled





MUMBAI: Umesh Chauhan (34), shot as a bystander during the attack on Tiger Shroff , survived thanks to the bullet’s unpredictable trajectory, said doctors. Dr Harish Pathak, dean of KEM Hospital, where Chauhan was operated on, said the bullet’s extreme heat during firing would have sterilised it.Surgeons said it entered the lower left chest, below the heart, passed through the liver, grazed the lung and struck a right-side rib. The impact deflected it without fracturing the rib, slowing it before it lodged in the right posterolateral back muscle, near but not touching the spine.“He is a very lucky man. The bullet’s movement, how it turned, where it hit, all made a difference,” said Dr Uday Jadhav, head of cardiovascular & thoracic surgery (CVTS). “Its final position allowed extraction through just a 1.5-cm incision. A different trajectory could have required major surgery or struck the heart, proving fatal.”The operation involved teams from general surgery, CVTS, pulmonary medicine, hepatology, cardiology, radiology and anaesthesiology. Dr Pathak said a bullet’s diameter determines only the entry wound, not the full extent of damage. Chauhan’s liver has begun healing. The father of a five-year-old, who is expecting another child in a few months, is likely to be discharged in about a week with painkillers and antibiotics.
Article Summary: Doctors say the bullet’s extreme heat during firing would have sterilised it. The impact deflected it without fracturing the rib, slowing it before it lodged in the right posterolateral back muscle, near but not touching the spine. A different trajectory could have required major surgery or struck the heart, proving fatal.

Article Title: Crude bomb? Battery-like object goes off in Bengaluru’s Pulikeshinagar flat, 2 hurt
Article Text:
The building where the blast took place





BENGALURU: A mysterious explosion inside an under-construction flat in east Bengaluru’s Pulikeshinagar has triggered a multi-agency investigation, with police suspecting that the materials involved were similar to those in a crude bomb.The blast, which injured two men Tuesday afternoon, has raised questions about how the device reached the site.City police, Internal Security Division (ISD), Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) and experts from the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) have joined the probe to establish the nature and cause of the explosion.A senior police officer told TOI that preliminary findings suggested the blast was not the kind of accidental electrical short circuit commonly reported in the city.The materials involved appeared similar to those used in a crude bomb, the officer said. Personal enmity was among the possible motives being explored.The explosion occurred in a fifth-floor flat where interior work was under way in a building owned by Abdul Rehman on Jeremiah Road.The injured were identified as Suraj Kumar , 23, a security guard, and Allauddin , 25, who was also present at the site.According to police sources, Suraj suffered injuries to one finger, an eye and his right hand, apart from burns on his face and neck.Allauddin also sustained burns on his face and neck. Both were initially taken to Bowring Hospital. Wednesday, Allauddin was discharged, while Suraj was shifted to Victoria Hospital.Initial statements from the injured men indicated that they had found a small, battery-like object lying on the street and brought it to the construction site out of curiosity.The device allegedly exploded when Suraj pressed a button on it. Investigators are, however, examining their accounts, which have reportedly contained contradictions.Police were alerted about the incident only Tuesday evening, when Bowring Hospital issued a medico-legal certificate to Pulikeshinagar police.Police commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh said several families lived in the building, where the explosion occurred in a vacant flat undergoing interior work.Police have recorded statements from the building owner and other occupants. The antecedents of the two injured men, who are from different states, are also being verified.Asked whether the incident could be terror-related, Singh said it was too early to draw conclusions. He assured residents there was no reason for panic.Home minister Priyank Kharge also urged the public not to pay heed to rumours until investigators received concrete findings.
Article Summary: Mysterious explosion inside under-construction flat in east Bengaluru triggers multi-agency investigation. Police suspect that the materials involved were similar to those in a crude bomb. Blast has raised questions about how the device reached the site. Personal enmity was among the possible motives being explored.

Article Title: 'No Jantar Mantar protest call promise': CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das let out of Tihar jail
Article Text:
Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were released from Tihar Jail after agreeing to certain conditions.





NEW DELHI: CJP 's Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were released from Tihar Jail on Wednesday after promising not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar.The two were ordered to be released after furnishing personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each and giving the undertaking before Special Executive Magistrate Ritu Raj, an ACP in Delhi Police."I undertake and promise not to commit any breach of peace... That we reiterate our undertaking... towards peace, law and order, public tranquillity and further we specifically state that we will not make any calls for protest at Jantar Mantar till such a time that it is de-notified," said their undertakings.They were detained after attempting to enter the barricaded Jantar Mantar protest site by climbing its gates on Oct 13 as part of their protest against SIR.The magistrate held that “further judicial custody does not appear to be necessary at this stage”, despite the investigating officer seeking a further three days of judicial custody, citing a continuing apprehension of a breach of peace.The magistrate held the risk of a breach of peace could be addressed through peace bonds and written assurances. The duo must appear at every hearing. The sureties will be verified before the next hearing on Oct 23.Prosecution led by counsel - Bhairav Dass and Prashant Prakash, argued that the duo’s statements to the court and the media were “contradictory”, and alleged that a CJP member’s media remarks while they were being taken to Tihar Jail on the previous hearing date undermined the “majesty of the SEM courts”.Advocates Abhik Chimni and Pranjal Abrol countered this with an unconditional verbal apology to the magistrate and reiterated the activists’ commitment to peace and said any protest would remain within the “four corners of Constitution”.Das and Ranka were first produced before the special executive magistrate on Oct 14 in preventive proceedings initiated by Parliament Street police over apprehensions that their conduct could disturb public tranquillity. They were sent to five days of judicial custody, extended by two days on Oct 19. The magistrate had rejected their earlier sureties, citing identification discrepancies and doubts about the sureties’ ability to ensure the activists’ presence.The duo challenged the Oct 19 order before HC, but withdrew the plea after the court advised them to await the outcome of the hearing scheduled before the magistrate.
Article Summary: CJP's Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were released from Tihar Jail on Wednesday. The two were ordered to be released after furnishing personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each. They were detained after attempting to enter the barricaded Jantar Mantar protest site by climbing its gates.

Article Title: Delhi HC to CJP duo: You're not Gen Z; lawyer says they are an inspiration
Article Text:
CJP co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka





NEW DELHI: Before being released by the special executive magistrate (SEM) late Wednesday evening, Cockroach Janta Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka faced several questions in Delhi High Court earlier in the day.The duo had approached the court challenging the extension of their judicial custody by the SEM and later withdrew the plea after the high court advised them to await the outcome of the hearing scheduled before the special executive magistrate and approach the appellate court if their grievance continues.Justice Subramonium Prasad of the high court observed that a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution was not an appropriate remedy for a “repeat case” of violating a peace bond.During the brief hearing, Justice Prasad made oral observations, voicing his concerns over the conduct of the two CJP members.The high court pointed out that the petitioners had violated a bond by entering a denotified protest site, and questioned if the police weren’t entitled to seek a “stricter” surety in a “repeat case”.Justice Prasad said once the petitioners “have broken peace for the second time, are the authorities not entitled to insist upon everything?”The court wondered if it should enter into the merits of the SEM’s decision or let “the events run their course.”The judge remarked that the questions surrounding the locus and motive of the petitioners were also significant and have to be examined, considering that while they were initially involved in a student protest, there was even a statement on “regime change” and this time, their cause was different.“Now there is another cause. People remain the same, causes change. All these questions assume significance. When the issue is breach of peace, it is important to know who you are; what is your motive, what are you trying to do, the purpose of your organisation. You suddenly hear something like ‘regime change’..... In a hearing like this, it is not necessary for us to go into this. Keep the debate for an appropriate proceeding,” the judge said.The counsel for the petitioners, advocate Abhik Chimni, sought the high court’s immediate intervention and argued that they ought to be released on a personal bond as the SEM has no jurisdiction to extend their judicial custody. He argued that the SEM’s insistence on a surety was not sustained in law.Justice Prasad told Chimni that “when there is apprehension of peace and tranquillity (being broken), all these questions will assume importance” and emphasised that the purpose behind police permission for a protest is not to stop anyone but prevent “unwanted persons” from joining a protest group and ensure that a peaceful agitation does not escalate into violence.“The two petitioners here are at the forefront. When you go and break a barricade, the chances of 10 or 20 more people violating the 163 (section on prohibitory order) are very bright. There might be persons who might not be in your control and who might do things. We have seen it happening outside our country. Students’ protests have now gone into arson, looting, burning,” the court said.The court sought to know the age of the petitioners and was informed that Das and Ranka were 27 and 31 years old, respectively. The court then remarked in a lighter vein, “That means you are not Gen Z.”“They are an inspiration,” their lawyer responded.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka faced several questions in Delhi High Court. The duo had approached the court challenging the extension of their judicial custody by the SEM. Justice Subramonium Prasad of the high court observed that a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution was not an appropriate remedy.

Article Title: Govt justifies buying MPA statue site, tells HC Shivaji is dear to Goans
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj is remembered by the people of Goa for his historical role against Portuguese colonialism

CS: Offer to buy encroached land was exploratory





PANAJI: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj has a "special place in the hearts and minds of the people of Goa" and "historically he was part of attempts to free Goa from the clutches of colonial Portuguese power", chief secretary V Candavelou has submitted to the high court, justifying state govt's proposal to buy the land encroached upon for erecting the statue on Mormugao Port Authority's (MPA) property in Feb.In an affidavit submitted to the high court, Candavelou stated that Shivaji came to Goa in 1683 to save its people from the oppressive Portuguese regime.I say that during the freedom movement of Goa, the people of Goa were inspired by the heroic attempts of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj to fight against the foreign invaders,” he stated.He said govt considered the matter at the highest administrative level in view of serious law and order concerns and intelligence inputs. It decided in principle to explore the feasibility of purchasing the land through mutual agreement to preserve public peace, avert an imminent mass agitation, with intelligence inputs indicating a potential gathering of 15,000 people, and prevent violent confrontation near the vital port establishment.Candavelou added that state govt did not endorse, condone, or encourage illegal encroachments or unauthorised constructions on public or private property.MPA had approached the high court over the alleged encroachment and unauthorised erection of the statue on its property. HC had criticised govt’s inaction and directed the police and govt authorities to assist MPA in removing the statue. MPA recently told the court that it wanted to withdraw its petition after the state expressed willingness to buy the land on which the statue was erected. The court subsequently directed the chief secretary to file a detailed affidavit.Candavelou said the letter informing MPA of the state’s approval to buy the land was an “exploratory effort in response to an acute public peace challenge” and was not intended to undermine the HC’s interim order.On the state bearing the cost of acquiring encroached private land, the chief secretary said the matter was “distinct in nature, involving a preliminary, non-statutory, exploratory exercise undertaken in good faith between two public entities, with the objective of maintaining public peace and harmony”.Candavelou gave an unqualified assurance that the state administration had acted in good faith under a compelling constitutional obligation to preserve public peace and harmony. He said the Sept 8 letter to MPA was preceded by continuous inter-departmental deliberations, field inspections and security assessments concerning the unauthorised statue.
Article Summary: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj came to Goa in 1683 to save its people from the oppressive Portuguese regime. Chief secretary V Candavelou said govt considered the matter at the highest administrative level in view of serious law and order concerns and intelligence inputs.

Article Title: Bishnoi gang link, Rs 2 lakh trail: Inside probe into Tiger Shroff attack case
Article Text:
The Mumbai police have taken into custody three more suspects in connection with the shooting incident involving Tiger Shroff





MUMBAI: The city crime branch on Wednesday arrested three more people in the case of firing at actor Tiger Shroff even as wanted criminal Shubham Lonkar of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang has allegedly emerged as a key executor of the plot.The total number of persons arrested in the case has now touched 10, including two women.The police are also probing if the accused had conducted reconnaissance of other Bollywood celebrities’ homes or whether Shroff was the only target.Lonkar’s name cropped up first in the city in the Oct 2024 killing of former NCP minister Baba Siddique in which he was alleged to have assembled shooters, supplied weapons and arranged finance.Lonkar’s brother Praveen is in jail in the Siddique murder case and the firing at Salman Khan ’s house in April 2024.Another key figure who has become the centre of the probe is Sameer, a garment shop owner from Sonipat, who coordinated with the shooters, police said.He was allegedly responsible for providing logistical support to the shooters. Police said that he stayed in Mumbai with the other accused and assisted them before returning from the city prior to the shooting.Preliminary ballistic reports have suggested the shooters used two country-made firearms which are yet to be recovered. The three accused shooters—Phool Singh (18), Rehan Ansari (18), and Rithik Mahtoo alias Roshan (22)—who were arrested from Kota were produced before the 37th Metropolitan Magistrate Court which remanded them to police custody till Oct 31.Police, while seeking police custody of the accused, told the court that the accused have destroyed the mobile phones used in connection with the crime, making the reconstruction of their communications through social media apps a key part of the investigation.Police are attempting to establish contact between the shooters and their alleged handlers through other digital evidence and their interrogation.The shooters had arrived in Mumbai on Sept 20, police said. “So far, investigation suggests the shooters and those who provided logistic support received around Rs 2 lakh, with which they bought a second-hand bike for Rs 25,000. Another Rs 37,000 was transferred in the account of Rehan Ansari. There were some more cash payments which are being ascertained,” said Raj Tilak Roshan, deputy commissioner of police. Investigators are also examining the payments made through UPI applications and cash.Ansari and Singh’s lawyer, Ajinkya Mirgal, argued that the police have already interrogated them in two days’ transit remand and they should be sent to judicial custody.According to the preliminary investigation, Anil Pandit allegedly contacted Sameer, who in turn allegedly contacted Ansari.Ansari is suspected of having brought together Phool Singh and Hrithik alias Roshan, the two accused alleged to have carried out the firing at Shroff.The five others, including two women, who have been arrested allegedly played roles in procuring, transporting and supplying weapons to the shooters and providing logistical support to the group. One of them, Radha, a bar dancer, was a friend of accused Kunal.The duo came to Mumbai along with Babita, another accused. While Kunal left Mumbai the same day, the two women stayed in an Andheri lodge, delivered the weapons, and left later. They are being brought to Mumbai and will be produced before a court on Thursday.
Article Summary: Mumbai police have taken into custody three more suspects in connection with the shooting incident involving Tiger Shroff. The total number of persons arrested in the case has now touched 10, including two women. The police are also probing if the accused had conducted reconnaissance of other Bollywood celebrities’ homes.

Article Title: Will water supply be smooth on Friday? Fears mount ahead of dry Thursday in Pune
Article Text:
Pune residents are bracing for another scheduled water cut while hoping for quicker restoration this time (AI image)

Officials from the Pune Municipal Corporation are working to improve the distribution network and address ongoing issues.





PUNE: As the city prepares for the Thursday water cut, residents hope for a smoother restoration than last week, when the single-day shutdown left many areas waiting hours, even days, for the supply to normalise.The concern goes beyond delayed restoration. Across several parts of Pune, residents said they had been battling low water pressure throughout the week, triggering shortages and forcing families to carefully ration whatever water they received.NCP (SP) member in Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) Kaka Chavan said the delayed restoration had once again exposed glaring weaknesses in the city’s water distribution network. “Citizens are unhappy with the low-pressure supply and poor management of distribution. Water is available in overhead tanks, yet many localities are not getting adequate supply. The problem is uneven distribution,” Chavan said.The issue has resonated beyond opposition benches. During the recent PMC general body meeting, several corporators voiced concerns over what they described as a worsening distribution crisis.Congress leader Chandu Kadam warned that the city was already struggling to recover from a single-day shutdown.“If Pune cannot restore normal supply after a one-day cut, how will it cope if harsher restrictions are imposed during late winter or peak summer? The administration must urgently take comprehensive steps to prevent a deeper water crisis,” he said.Those fears are not unfounded. The irrigation department has already suggested stricter restrictions further by moving from a weekly shutdown to an alternate-day supply model, effectively leaving residents without water for three to four days every week. While PMC sources said such a drastic step was not immediately on the cards, they acknowledged that restrictions could be intensified gradually if the situation deteriorated.For residents who are already struggling, the prospect is alarming. Aundh resident Punit Kadam said the civic authorities must focus on three priorities after every shutdown — ensuring water reaches all areas by Friday afternoon, increasing supply volumes on Friday and boosting pressure across the network. “The authorities also need to closely monitor valve operations so that every locality gets its fair share of water,” he said.Hadapsar resident Amey Satav alleged that citizens were effectively facing hidden water cuts already. “PMC has indirectly imposed additional restrictions by reducing pressure in the distribution lines,” he alleged.Facing mounting criticism, officials from PMC’s water supply department said teams had been working to clear bottlenecks in the network and improve distribution. They expressed confidence that the restoration exercise following Thursday’s shutdown would be quicker and more efficient.The residents, however, said confidence in supply would be restored only when the taps started flowing again.
Article Summary: Pune residents are bracing for another scheduled water cut while hoping for quicker restoration this time. Across several parts of Pune, residents said they had been battling low water pressure throughout the week, triggering shortages. The irrigation department has already suggested stricter restrictions further by moving from a weekly shutdown to an alternate-day supply model.

Article Title: How a domestic dispute led 2 brothers to strangle their father, burn his body with petrol and bury it near home
Article Text:
Two brothers named Shiv and Deependra have been arrested for allegedly murdering their father.





JHUNJHUNU: Police Tuesday arrested two brothers for allegedly strangling their father, burning his body with petrol and burying it near their house at Tara ka Bas village in Jhunjhunu’s Sultana police station area.Sultana SHO Ramniwas said preliminary investigation indicated that Shiv and Deependra had allegedly killed their father, Jugal Kishore Jangid, during a domestic dispute. They allegedly told relatives and others that he had gone to Mumbai and claimed that the buried remains belonged to an unidentified person.Police received information on Oct 17, 2026 about a body buried near a house in the village. An FSL team examined the site, and the body was identified as Jugal Kishore.His cousin, Pawan Kumar, lodged a report on Oct 18. Questioning of family members revealed that Jugal Kishore had been missing for six to seven days. Police registered a case on suspicion that he had been murdered and buried.Chirawa DSP Gaurav Gurjar inspected the scene, while MIU and MOB teams collected scientific evidence. A team led by Ramniwas investigated the case using technical evidence and intelligence inputs.Police said suspicion subsequently fell on Jugal Kishore’s sons. They were detained for questioning and arrested after facts concerning the incident emerged.According to Ramniwas, the brothers allegedly strangled their father in a fit of rage, poured petrol on his body, burnt it and buried it in the soil near their house. The killing was believed to have occurred five to seven days before the body was found.A court remanded both accused in police custody for three days. Police are investigating the material allegedly used in the crime and other aspects of the case.
Article Summary: Two brothers named Shiv and Deependra have been arrested for allegedly murdering their father. Police received information on Oct 17, 2026 about a body buried near a house in the village. An FSL team examined the site, and the body was identified as Jugal Kishore.

Article Title: 21 IIT-Bombay faculty members condemn ‘unprecedented’ police action against protesting students, seek explanation from institute director
Article Text:
Twenty-one IIT-Bombay faculty members wrote to the director condemning police actions against protesting students.





MUMBAI: As many as 21 IIT-Bombay faculty members have written to the institute’s director, condemning what they called ‘unprecedented’ police action against students peacefully protesting on campus on Sunday and seeking an explanation.A small section of students have been protesting for over a month after second-year B Tech student Sahil Wakode died by suicide on Sept 18. They have been demanding action and accountability from the institute since then.The letter, sent on Monday, came a day after students were twice detained from the campus protest site, dubbed as ‘Justice Corner’. Police also allegedly dismantled the protest site, removing banners and posters. Sahil’s parents, Ravindra and Sonali Wakode, who visited the institute to pay homage to him alleged they were forcibly taken to Azad Maidan police station and detained till 6pm.The faculty members, in the letter, sought to know whether any institute functionary had authorised police action. If not, they asked whether the administration would seek an FIR against the police officers responsible for the “act of violence” committed against the students.At the outset, the faculty members acknowledged differing views on the ongoing protest, with some considering it irrelevant or damaging to IIT-B’s reputation, while others viewed it as a necessary call for the institute to reflect on its educational commitments and responsibilities amid its history of student suicides. They condemned the forceful removal of students who have been peacefully protesting for several weeks.The faculty members sought explanations from the administration regarding who authorised police to enter the campus and detain students, the use of ‘brute force’ during both rounds of detention, and the alleged failure of institute officials to intervene or help the detainees. “We have learnt that students detained at the police station tried to contact the dean of student affairs, Quick Response Team and chief security officer for help, but their requests were not entertained and that no institute functionary came to the police station. What accounts for it?” they asked.They also questioned the alleged vandalism at the protest site, which displayed images of Jyotirao Phule, Savitribai Phule, and Dr B R Ambedkar. They sought an explanation for the administration’s refusal to return students’ personal belongings, including laptops, and asked whether due procedure had been followed in seizing them.IIT-B authorities did not comment on the letter.Sources claimed that police had come to the campus only because Congress MP Varsha Gaikwad planned to visit that day. The institute had not responded to the MP’s letter seeking permission, and her visit coincided with a visit by Wakode’s parents.Sources also claimed that students jeering at police minutes before Gaikwad and Wakode’s parents arrived had prompted the detentions. Regarding the confiscation of personal belongings, they claimed that the items were lying at the gate and blocking the entrance. The institute plans to return them to the students in accordance with its lost-and-found SOP, they added.
Article Summary: 21 IIT-Bombay faculty members have written to the institute’s director condemning what they called ‘unprecedented’ police action. A small section of students have been protesting for over a month after second-year B Tech student Sahil Wakode died by suicide on Sept 18. They have been demanding action and accountability from the institute.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff firing: Rs 2 lakh paid to shooters, logistics team, cops trace UPI transfers; 2 factory-made firearms not recovered yet
Article Text:
Three individuals were arrested in connection to the firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff and brought to Mumbai.





MUMBAI: The three persons allegedly involved in the firing at actor Tiger Shroff were brought back to Mumbai from Kota on Wednesday morning and remanded in police custody till Oct 31.Preliminary ballistic reports have suggested the shooters while firing at actor Tiger Shroff used two factory-made firearms which are yet to be recovered. The three accused shooters-Phool Singh (18), Rehan Ansari (18), and Rithik Kumar alias Roshan (22)-who were arrested from Kota were produced before the 37th Metropolitan Magistrate Court which remanded them to police custody till Oct 31.Cops, while seeking police custody of the accused, told the court that the accused have destroyed the mobile phones used in connection with the crime, making the reconstruction of their communications through social media apps a key part of the investigation.Police are attempting to establish contact between the shooters and their alleged handlers, including Shubham Lonkar, through other digital evidence and their interrogation.The shooters had arrived in Mumbai on Sept 20, police said. "So far, investigation suggests the shooters and those who provided logistic support received around Rs 2 lakh, with which they bought a second-hand bike for Rs 25,000. Another Rs 37,000 was transferred in the account of Rehan Ansari.There were some more cash payments which are being ascertained," said Raj Tilak Roshan, deputy commissioner of police. Investigators are also examining the payments made through UPI applications and cash.Ansari and Singh's lawyer, Ajinkya Mirgal, argued that the police have already interrogated them in two days' transit remand and they should be sent to judicial custody.According to the preliminary investigation, Anil Pandit allegedly contacted Sameer, who also allegedly contacted Ansari.Ansari is suspected of having brought together Phool Singh and Rithik Kumar, the two accused alleged to have carried out the firing at Shroff.The five others, including two women, who have been arrested allegedly played roles in procuring, transporting and supplying weapons to the shooters and providing logistical support to the group. One of them, Radha, a bar girl, was a friend of accused Kunal. The duo came to Mumbai along with Babita, another accused. While Kunal left Mumbai the same day, the two women stayed in an Andheri lodge, delivered the weapons, and left later. They are being brought to Mumbai and will be produced before a court on Thursday.Sources associated with the probe suggested the accused monitored Shroff's movements through social media posts, videos and reels shared by the actor and his fans. The accused had done a survey of this playground in Juhu for 10 days. The shooters had even laid out a plan on Oct 11 but the actor did not turn up.
Article Summary: Three individuals were arrested in connection to the firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff and brought to Mumbai. The three accused shooters-Phool Singh (18), Rehan Ansari (18) and Rithik Kumar alias Roshan (22)-who were arrested from Kota were produced before the 37th Metropolitan Magistrate Court which remanded them to police custody till Oct 31.

Article Title: Video: Kanpur man dies after attackers trap hands in car windows, drag him on roof for 1.5km
Article Text:
A 37-year-old man, Biru Singh Bhadauriya, died after being assaulted in Kanpur's Hanumant Vihar area.

Poll Vote & Share your view What measures could help prevent such violent incidents? Stronger patrolling and surveillance Stricter action against violent offenders 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





KANPUR: A 37-year-old man died on Wednesday after he was allegedly assaulted, pinned to the roof of a car with his hands trapped between its window panes and dragged for around 1.5km by a group of attackers in Kanpur’s Hanumant Vihar area.Police are examining CCTV footage as part of the investigation.The incident took place on Tuesday night when Biru Singh Bhadauriya was returning home after visiting a Dussehra fair. The attackers allegedly rammed their car into him over an old rivalry before assaulting him and forcing him onto the vehicle’s roof.They allegedly trapped both his hands between the window panes, shut the windows and drove at high speed for around 1.5km with Bhadauriya on the roof. The attackers then allegedly threw him onto the road and fled.Bhadauriya was rushed to Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital, where he died during treatment on Wednesday.According to a post on the official Kanpur Commissionerate police handle, a man was seriously injured after being hit by an unidentified vehicle on Arra Road on Tuesday night. He succumbed to his injuries during treatment at Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital the following day.Police said a case had been registered under relevant sections and the postmortem examination had been conducted. Further legal action is underway, with investigators examining CCTV footage to establish the sequence of events and identify those involved.
Article Summary: Biru Singh Bhadauriya, 37, died after being assaulted in Kanpur's Hanumant Vihar area. He was allegedly pinned to the roof of a car with his hands trapped between its window panes and dragged for around 1.5km by a group of attackers. Police are examining CCTV footage as part of the investigation.

Article Title: Unnao murder mystery: How woman and YouTuber friend killed her husband in room, stuffed his body in box and transported 21km away
Article Text:
(AI IMAGE) Unnao police solved a murder case involving the body of a man found in a box on a highway.





KANPUR: Unnao police have solved the murder of a young man whose body was found locked inside a box on a highway service lane and arrested his 28-year-old wife, Neha Rawat, and YouTuber Jitendra alias Rahul Singh for allegedly killing him.According to police, Neha and Jitendra allegedly killed Sonu Savita (28) at his rented room in Kanchan Nagar, Shuklaganj, on Monday night before transporting the body 21 km to Lalaookheda in the Sadar area.CCTV footage helped police trace the loader used to transport the box. Investigators found that the vehicle’s driver had no role in the crime.Police said Jitendra allegedly consumed alcohol with Sonu from around 9 pm. Around midnight, after Sonu became heavily intoxicated, Neha allegedly struck him on the head with a grinding stone (sil-batta). She and Jitendra then allegedly assaulted him with bamboo sticks and smothered him with a blanket, causing his death.Around 6 pm on Tuesday, Jitendra allegedly paid Rs 10,000 to two labourers, including a minor to help move the box.The accused allegedly hired a loader for Rs 1,200 and misled its driver by claiming they were shifting accommodation.Neha and the two labourers travelled in the vehicle and unloaded the box on the service lane of the Unnao-Lalganj highway around 8 pm. A bulldozer repair shop operator noticed it about an hour later and informed police.Sonu, a resident of Panchamkheda village in Hasanganj, had met Neha nine years ago. Police said she later left her husband, Jagdish, and four daughters and moved in with Sonu in Shuklaganj. After living together for two years, the couple solemnised a court marriage.Investigators said Neha later became close to Jitendra, who had rented a room in the same house.SP Jaiprakash Singh said the preliminary investigation indicated that the deceased’s wife and her YouTuber friend were involved in the murder. Two other individuals have also been detained, and further legal proceedings are under way, he added.
Article Summary: Unnao police have solved the murder of a young man whose body was found locked inside a box on a highway service lane. Police arrested his 28-year-old wife, Neha Rawat, and YouTuber Jitendra alias Rahul Singh for allegedly killing him.

Article Title: 15-year-old girl raped by 3 men after running away from home in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
A distressing event unfolded when a 15-year-old girl fled her home in Tirunelveli after a family dispute (Representative image)





MADURAI: Two men were arrested for raping a 15-year-old girl stranded in Tiruchendur after running away from home. Two minor boys have also been booked under Pocso Act The Class X student had left her home in Tirunelveli on Oct 15 after arguing with her parents over failing an exam, said police. When she did not return, the parents lodged a ‘missing person’ complaint with the Thalaiyuthu police.The girl had boarded a train to Tiruchendur with her boyfriend and another friend. The boys harassed her during the trip, said police. After learning from their parents that police were after them, they handed her some money and abandoned her.At Tiruchendur, three men from Madurai — Karthik Shanmugasundaram and Mani — approached her, offering assistance. They took her to Kulasekarapattinam where a Dasara festival was under way. Mani, 28, raped her before leaving town with Shanmugasundaram.Police said the men had gone to the fest to commit theft.Karthik, 26, a divorcee, promised to marry her and took her to his house in Vadipatti on Oct 16, and raped her, said police. She escaped with help from locals and reached Mattuthavani bus stand in Madurai.Tirunelveli police traced her to Vadipatti, and rescued her from Mattuthavani on Oct 17. Police had used CCTV footage and facial recognition to trace the whereabouts of the girl and the three men.Mani and Shanmugasundaram were remanded in judicial custody on Tuesday. Karthik was remanded by the Dindigul police. Police said the two minors would be produced before Juvenile Justice Board and sent to an observation home.
Article Summary: The Class X student had left her home in Tirunelveli on Oct 15 after arguing with her parents over failing an exam. When she did not return, the parents lodged a ‘missing person’ complaint with the Thalaiyuthu police. Two minor boys have also been booked under Pocso Act.

Article Title: Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest U-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik killed in late-night road accident on Cuttack highway
Article Text:
Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati and Malay Barik, two talented athletes from Odisha, tragically lost their lives in an accident





BHUBANESWAR: Two promising Odisha athletes, Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest under-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik, were killed in a road accident on the Cuttack highway late Wednesday night.Dondapati had emerged as one of the country's fastest sprinters in the under-23 category in 2025, while Barik competed in the 400m event. Their deaths have left Odisha's sporting fraternity mourning the loss of two young athletes.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi expressed grief over their deaths in a social media post."Deeply saddened by the tragic demise of athletes Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati and Malaya Barik in a road accident. Their untimely passing is a profound loss to Odisha's sporting fraternity," Majhi said.Offering condolences to the bereaved families, he prayed to Mahaprabhu Shri Jagannath to give them strength to cope with the loss and grant eternal peace to the departed souls.
Article Summary: Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest under-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik, were killed in a road accident on the Cuttack highway late Wednesday night. Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi expressed grief over their deaths.

MUMBAI: Investigations into the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff have revealed that the accused allegedly practised shooting at a location near Mumbai before carrying out the attack.Crime Branch officials said the accused identified the location where they had tested the firearm during interrogation. One of them allegedly fired two rounds, while another fired one round to check whether the weapon was functioning properly.Police have also learnt that the firearm accidentally went off while being tested inside a hotel room in Andheri, with the bullet hitting the bed.Based on information gathered during interrogation, police are examining the alleged firing practice site near Mumbai and investigating the preparations made before the incident.Meanwhile, Mumbai Police arrested two more suspects in connection with the firing case on Wednesday, taking the total number of arrests to 10. The two accused are expected to be produced before a court in Sonipat, Haryana, to seek transit remand. Once the court grants approval, they will be brought to Mumbai for further questioning.According to reports, the two suspects allegedly played a significant role in supplying weapons linked to the case.Investigators are probing their links with the other accused and their alleged involvement in planning and executing the incident.In another development, investigators will examine an audio clip containing a threat allegedly directed at Tiger Shroff. Officials plan to compare the voice in the recording with voice samples maintained in databases by the Punjab and Delhi Police.These databases reportedly contain recordings of individuals allegedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Police units in Punjab, Delhi and Rajasthan maintain separate collections of voice samples that can help verify the identities of suspected speakers.Similar verification procedures have previously been undertaken in investigations involving audio clips linked to threats allegedly received by actor Salman Khan, actor Aamir Khan, filmmaker Rohit Shetty and the late politician Baba Siddique, among others.Investigators are examining the available audio evidence and other leads to establish the identities of those involved and determine the extent of their alleged roles in the firing case.

Article Title: Over 3 lakh Punjab govt employees continue mass leave on day-3 as talks fail; bus staff extend strike indefinitely
Article Text:
Bus staff protest in Patiala on Wednesday





CHANDIGARH: Over three lakh Punjab govt employees took mass casual leave on Wednesday over pending demands, disrupting work across govt offices. Talks with the state govt failed to break the deadlock, with employees deciding to continue their two-day protest on Thursday. Meanwhile, the Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers’ Union extended its statewide strike indefinitely, affecting bus services.Employee representatives met chief secretary KAP Sinha at 4 pm after the govt released minutes of an earlier meeting with chief minister Bhagwant Mann, as demanded by unions. However, the nearly two-hour meeting remained inconclusive.Sukhchain Singh Khaira, coordinator of the Joint Action Committee leading the agitation, said work across govt offices, including directorates, was affected. Sahil Sharma, general secretary of the Punjab Civil Secretariat Employees Union, alleged the govt was delaying a resolution by asking unions to reiterate demands already raised in previous meetings.A 39-member delegation of employees and pensioners later met officials but said it received no clear assurances on several demands. They said the govt had clarified that temporary teachers described as regularised had only been given “security of tenure”, without the financial benefits available to regular employees.The delegation also said the govt had no roadmap for Anganwadi, ASHA and mid-day meal workers.The future course of the agitation will be decided at a meeting in Ludhiana on Oct 25. Employees are demanding release of pending dearness allowance (DA) instalments and arrears, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), regularisation of contractual staff, revision of pensions, restoration of 37 discontinued allowances and the cashless health scheme. They have also sought withdrawal of notifications imposing central pay scales and a three-year probation period.The standoff continues despite a Sept 18 meeting between Mann and employee and pensioner representatives, when the chief minister announced an 8% DA hike in two instalments of 4% each from Oct 1 and promised regular monthly meetings.Meanwhile, transport workers extended their strike after talks with a cabinet minister failed to resolve demands for regularisation under service rules, direct departmental contracts for outsourced workers and withdrawal of police cases linked to earlier protests.Union general secretary Shamsher Singh said proposals covering around 1,400 outsourced Punjab Roadways employees and more than 1,700 PRTC workers remained pending. A Sept 21 govt letter had set a one-month deadline to shift workers from outsourcing agencies to direct contracts, but it passed without implementation, he said. A proposal to withdraw cases had also been sent to the Punjab DGP, but no further action had followed despite workers securing bail.The union plans a joint demonstration with Theka Mulazam Sangharsh Morcha in Dirba, the constituency of transport and finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema. Workers from all 27 depots and two sub-depots plan to assemble in Mohali and march towards Punjab Vidhan Sabha and the chief minister’s official residence.Union representatives alleged that shortages of spare parts and tyres had grounded several buses and criticised PRTC management for issuing show-cause notices and termination warnings. However, PRTC GM Operations A S Tiwana said more than 800 of the corporation’s 1,250 buses operated on Wednesday. He said management had proposed bringing around 1,719 outsourced employees under contractual terms.Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh called the mass leave a sign of a deepening crisis of confidence between the Mann govt and its employees. He demanded immediate talks and time-bound solutions, accusing the govt of prioritising publicity over public grievances.
Article Summary: Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers’ Union extended its statewide strike indefinitely, affecting bus services. Talks with the state govt failed to break the deadlock, with employees deciding to continue their two-day protest on Thursday.

Article Title: Mettur Dam water release for Cauvery delta irrigation to end tonight after 45 days
Article Text:
The Mettur Dam





SALEM: Water release from Mettur Dam for irrigation in the Cauvery delta will stop on Thursday night, as the 45-day schedule that began on September 1 comes to an end.Chief minister C Joseph Vijay opened the dam for irrigation after reservoir levels improved following inflows from catchment areas in Karnataka. The water level stood at about 91.56 feet against the dam’s full capacity of 120 feet when releases began. The schedule was intended to support irrigation across the Cauvery delta region.On Thursday morning, the reservoir level stood at 59.13 feet, down from about 91.56 feet on September 1. Storage was recorded at 24.04 tmc ft, while inflow had fallen to 696 cusecs.Water Resources Department (WRD) officials said the dam’s storage levels and future inflows would determine any further decisions on irrigation releases.
Article Summary: Water release from Mettur Dam for irrigation in the Cauvery delta will stop on Thursday night. The 45-day schedule that began on September 1 comes to an end. Chief minister C Joseph Vijay opened the dam for irrigation after reservoir levels improved following inflows from Karnataka.

Article Title: 7 years apart, anti-drug activist Parvinder Jhota’s killing revives memories of Neha Shoree murder
Article Text:
Neha Shoree, Parvinder Jhota (File Photos)

Neha Shoree: A licence cancelled and then a killing

Parvinder Singh Jhota: The 2023 dispute that preceded his killing

A continuing challenge for Punjab





CHANDIGARH: Seven years after Punjab drug licensing officer Neha Shoree was shot dead in her office, the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa has brought renewed attention to the risks faced by those who challenge alleged illegal drug sales in the state.The two cases, separated by more than seven years, involved different circumstances and accused persons. But both brought allegations of illegal drug sales into focus and raised questions about the enforcement of laws governing medicines and addictive substances.Shoree, a zonal licensing drug authority, was shot dead in her office in Kharar near Mohali on March 29, 2019. Jhota, 45, was shot dead in Mansa on October 13, 2026, while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs.Four other people were injured in the firing, which was captured during Jhota’s Facebook Live broadcast.Shoree was selected as a drug inspector through the Punjab Public Service Commission in 2007 and joined the health department in Ropar that October. In 2013, she was given the responsibility of district zonal licensing authority.On March 29, 2019, she was shot dead at her office by Balwinder Singh, a chemist from Morinda whose shop licence she had cancelled in 2009, police said.During her tenure as a drug inspector in Ropar, Shoree had raided shops and seized banned drugs.Her parents alleged that the drug mafia was behind the killing because she had exposed the sale of intoxicants in the Ropar and Kharar region.“We want to question Prime Minister Narendra Modi that you have been assuring to make a drug-free country but here women officers are being killed by drug mafia,” her mother and paternal aunt said, according to a TOI report published on March 31, 2019.The family’s allegations prompted demands for a wider investigation. The then Punjab chief minister, Capt Amarinder Singh, subsequently handed the probe to ADGP Prabodh Kumar, director of the Bureau of Investigation.However, in December 2019, police informed the Punjab and Haryana high court that their investigation had found no involvement of the drug mafia or any other person besides the accused.Shoree’s family continued to question the findings and seek further investigation.In September 2019, the Punjab government approved financial benefits of around Rs 31 lakh for her family. Shoree’s killing had also prompted scrutiny of the licensing process and the circumstances surrounding the accused’s arms licence.Jhota became known in Mansa for confronting medical store owners whom he accused of selling intoxicating pills, synthetic drugs and other prohibited substances. He recorded confrontations and shared videos on social media.His dispute with medical store owner Ashwani Kumar dated back to July 2023. Jhota had allegedly put a garland of shoes around Kumar’s neck in a public confrontation, accusing him of selling synthetic drugs.A case was registered against Jhota, who was arrested and spent nearly two months in jail. He was released on September 11, 2023, after the complainant approached the court to withdraw the complaint.The case against Kumar concerning the alleged sale of prohibited substances remained pending.Jhota continued his campaign. On the morning of October 13, 2026, he reportedly met an elderly man who had bought synthetic drugs from a medical store and took him to Kumar’s shop to question the owner about the alleged sale.The confrontation escalated as Jhota livestreamed it on Facebook. Kumar allegedly pulled out a firearm and opened fire inside the shop before following the injured activist into the street and firing again. Jhota was hit by three bullets and died at Mansa Civil Hospital. Four others were also injured.In the video, Jhota is heard saying, “maar mainu, maar mainu” (kill me).Kumar fled after the shooting and was arrested in Rajasthan’s Salasar on October 14. Police also detained an alleged associate accused of helping him escape.Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, a retired Army serviceman, refused to cremate his son until those responsible were brought to justice.“I am still alive and pledge to fight against the drug peddlers as my son was waging a war against them. I am also ready to take a bullet if the peddlers are not taken to task,” Bhim Singh said at Mansa Civil Hospital.The killings have brought renewed attention to the state’s efforts to curb drug abuse and the alleged illegal sale of addictive pharmaceutical substances. Following Jhota’s murder, the Punjab government stepped up inspections of chemist shops.The two cases must be viewed in their individual contexts: Shoree was a government officer carrying out licensing duties, while Jhota was an activist who publicly confronted people he accused of selling prohibited substances.Investigators in Shoree’s case said they found no evidence of anyone else being involved in her murder, while the investigation into Jhota’s killing concerns a separate accused and a separate dispute.Their deaths, years apart, have nevertheless renewed questions about the availability of addictive substances, the enforcement of drug-sale regulations and the safety of people who seek to expose alleged violations.
Article Summary: Neha Shoree, a zonal licensing drug authority, was shot dead in her office in Kharar near Mohali on March 29, 2019. Parvinder Singh Jhota, 45, was killed in Mansa on October 13, 2026, while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs. Both cases, separated by more than seven years, involved different circumstances and accused persons.

Article Title: ‘Don’t trouble me, I’ll commit suicide’: Absconding in Shiva Sharma death case, model Shraddha Dubey releases another video
Article Text:
Shraddha Dubey, accused of killing her businessman boyfriend, Shiva Sharma, has released another.

The 1st video





LUCKNOW: Model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, named as the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma in Lucknow, has released another video on Thursday claiming that the two had been dating for the past two months and that Sharma was under a massive debt.In the five-minute-long video, Dubey recounted the events leading up to Sharma’s death.Dubey alleged that Sharma had been receiving calls from people he had borrowed money from and had repeatedly told her that he would die by suicide if he could not repay the loans.She said she could show screenshots to support her claims.In the video, Dubey also appealed to people to stop harassing her, warning that she would die by suicide if the alleged torture continued.“Think why would someone kill someone and throw them from their own apartment,” she said, questioning the allegations against her.She urged the media not to spread rumours without evidence. Referring to Sharma’s mother, Dubey alleged that she had started a quarrel with her driver in the hospital. She then said, “It's not like you have lost a son, I have lost my boyfriend.”Dubey claimed that she and Sharma had not spoken to each other for six to seven days before the incident.On October 7, Sharma allegedly contacted her driver through a tea vendor and was crying, she said."Then I called him twice from my number. He did not pick up the call at that time. Later, he called me around 2am. I asked him what happened to which he asked me to meet him. We met, went to cafe where he ordered coffee for me and juice for himself," she said, adding that he had a "lot of beers" before meeting her."Later, both of us went to my place. While he drove my car, my driver took his car," she said.Dubey said her sister, Rashmi, visited her home on October 8 to discuss a puja for Navratri. She denied her sister's involvement in the case, claiming that Rashmi barely knew Sharma and had hardly spoken to him."My sister has nothing to do with this case. She did not even know Shiva that well. She never spoke to him...My sister and I, we went for a walk that evening. Shiva's friends joined us - one of them was Ashwini Mishra and other named Harsh. We all went for a long drive. I spoke to Shiva, his mother, brother-in-law, and sister too that day," she said.Recounting the day Sharma died, Dubey claimed that he appeared depressed on October 9. She said they woke up and made tea before he went to the washroom."I don't even know what it was. We woke up, made tea. Shiva went to the washroom. Usually, he would never close the main gate. But this time, he did. I asked my sister to go check up on him after a while. As soon as she opened the gate, he jumped from the balcony," she said.Dubey alleged that Sharma's mother accused them of murder and assaulted her driver when she arrived at the hospital."It will be recorded on the hospital's camera. Without knowing anything, she accused us of murder. Without thinking, she blamed us for murder. She blamed us so badly that we might not be able to get out of that blame for life," she said.Earlier, Dubey had released another video denying any wrongdoing and claiming that Sharma’s death was a case of suicide, not murder.She also urged the media to stop linking her to politicians and senior officials, saying she was willing to appear before the police and record her statement.“Just because someone follows me or is connected to me on Instagram does not mean I know them or have any relationship with them,” she had said.Dubey had also denied being absconding and claimed she wanted to cooperate with investigators.“I am not missing. I want to come before the police and tell them everything I know. I want to place the complete truth before them,” she said in the earlier video.Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area. According to police sources, he had been in a relationship with Dubey for around four months.Following his death, Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, lodged an FIR accusing Dubey, her sister Rashmi, driver Adil and others of murdering her son. The family has alleged that Dubey pushed Sharma from the building, a claim investigators are examining.Lucknow Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and Tanveer Ali alias Danish in connection with the case.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey claims her boyfriend, Shiva Sharma, was under a massive debt. Dubey says Sharma had been receiving calls from people he had borrowed money from and had repeatedly told her that he would die by suicide if he could not repay the loans. Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of his apartment in Lucknow.

Palantir has a message for Europe on technology dependence. Louis Mosley, the head of Palantir Technologies' UK and Europe operations, has argued that European countries will have to accept some reliance on US technology, at least in the short term, even as governments explore alternatives to American software providers. He also pointed to Europe's dependence on China for industrial components, particularly magnets required to manufacture drones.Speaking to Bloomberg News in Brussels, Mosley argued that Europe's dependence on China for industrial supplies also deserves greater attention, particularly as countries seek to strengthen their defence capabilities and expand drone production.he said.Mosley added that European countries would have to recognise the limits of their efforts to become technologically self-sufficient. He said,His comments come at a time when European governments are seeking more technological independence from strained relations across the Atlantic and growing fears about access to sensitive data.A handful of countries have reviewed their contracts with Palantir, but practical needs, especially in defence, make it hard for Europe to do away with foreign technology providers entirely, Mosley said.Palantir provides customised data analysis software to governments and organisations, including civilian agencies, intelligence services, police forces and militaries. The company, valued at more than $480 billion, has expanded its role in defence technology through products that use artificial intelligence to analyse information and support military operations.In 2025, NATO's military branch agreed with Palantir to deploy its Maven Smart System, which uses AI for surveillance and targeting.Mosley described the system asarguing that further cooperation on data sharing and integration could benefit NATO members.The system illustrates the role that American technology companies play in European defence infrastructure, even as governments discuss reducing their reliance on foreign suppliers.Palantir's position in Europe has faced challenges since Donald Trump 's return to the US presidency last year strained transatlantic relations and increased scrutiny of American technology companies.Chief Executive Officer Alex Karp has cultivated close ties with the Trump administration and promoted a strong pro-American position. This has contributed to concerns among some European leaders about relying on US companies for sensitive government operations.In June, France announced that its domestic intelligence agency would end its Palantir contract in favour of a local provider. British lawmakers have also criticised the company's work with the UK's health system.These developments have created opportunities for European technology companies seeking to replace American providers.
